name: Liar's poker
summary: Bar game where players bid on how many times a digit appears across all hidden dollar bill serial numbers.
rules_text: Each player holds a US dollar bill and secretly looks at its eight-digit serial number. Digits are ranked 1 high as ace, then 0, 9, 8, down to 2 low. The starting player bids a quantity and a digit value, claiming at least that many of that digit occur across all bills. In clockwise order, each next player must either raise the bid by bidding a higher digit at the same quantity, or any digit at a higher quantity, or challenge the previous bid. When a bid is challenged, all bills are revealed and the digit is counted. If the count is at least the bid, the bidder wins a dollar from each other player; if not, the bidder loses a dollar to each other player. A round ends after a challenge.
rating_reason: Specific bluffing bidding game with hidden bills, pure reasoning
